content.text:
Feature: Track time and per-job pay in one system
  As a cleaning business owner, I want cleaner clock-in/out and per-job pay (hourly or piece-rate) tracked in the same system as scheduling, with a payroll-ready export, so that I stop running a parallel time-tracking system and pay disputes disappear. (Research: owners maintain separate clock-in systems; no payroll integration is a named ZenMaid gap — pain-points §1.3, §4)
  Rule: Worked time is recorded when a cleaner clocks in on arrival and clocks out on completion of a job assigned to them.
    Scenario: Cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job
      Given a job assigned to cleaner Maria scheduled for today
      When Maria taps clock in on arrival at 9:00 and clock out at 11:30 on completion
      Then a time entry of 2 hours 30 minutes is recorded against that job for Maria

    Scenario: Cleaner tries to clock in on a job not assigned to them
      Given a job that is not assigned to cleaner Maria
      When Maria attempts to clock in on that job
      Then the clock-in is rejected and no time entry is recorded

  Rule: Each job's pay is calculated from its configured pay model: hourly pay equals the cleaner's rate times worked hours, and per-job pay is a fixed piece rate regardless of time.
    Scenario: Hourly job pays rate times worked hours
      Given an hourly job with Maria's rate set to $25 per hour
      When Maria records 2 hours 30 minutes of worked time on the job
      Then the job's gross pay is calculated as $62.50

    Scenario: Per-job piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time
      Given a per-job job with a piece rate of $80
      When Maria completes the job in 2 hours on one visit and another cleaner would take 3 hours
      Then the job's gross pay is $80 regardless of the worked time recorded

  Rule: A pay period accumulates each cleaner's gross earnings into a running total across all their jobs.
    Scenario: Running pay-period total builds as jobs complete
      Given a pay period in progress for Maria with an hourly job paying $62.50 already recorded
      When Maria completes a second per-job job paying $80 in the same pay period
      Then Maria's running pay-period total shows $142.50

  Rule: The owner can export a pay period as a payroll-ready CSV listing each cleaner's hours, jobs, and gross pay.
    Scenario: Owner exports a completed pay period to CSV
      Given a closed pay period with all time entries resolved for three cleaners
      When the owner exports the pay period
      Then a CSV downloads with one row per cleaner showing worked hours, job count, and gross pay ready for the payroll provider

  Rule: A time entry with no clock-out is flagged for owner review and excluded from pay totals and export until the owner resolves it.
    Scenario: Cleaner forgets to clock out
      Given Maria clocked in at 9:00 and left the job without clocking out
      When the owner opens the pay period for review
      Then the open time entry is flagged for review, is excluded from Maria's pay total, and the owner can set the missing clock-out time to resolve it

    Scenario: Export blocked while an unresolved time entry remains
      Given a pay period that still contains one flagged open time entry
      When the owner attempts to export the pay period to CSV
      Then the owner is warned that unresolved time entries exist and the export excludes or blocks until the entry is resolved

# QA Story 838: Track time and per-job pay in one system

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning business owner, I want cleaner clock-in/out and per-job pay (hourly or piece-rate) tracked in the same system as scheduling, with a payroll-ready export, so that I stop running a parallel time-tracking system and pay disputes disappear. (Research: owners maintain separate clock-in systems; no payroll integration is a named ZenMaid gap — pain-points §1.3, §4)

## Acceptance criteria

- Cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job
- Cleaner tries to clock in on a job not assigned to them
- Hourly job pays rate times worked hours
- Per-job piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time
- Running pay-period total builds as jobs complete
- Owner exports a completed pay period to CSV
- Cleaner forgets to clock out

task first.

# Qa Story Brief

Per-story QA testing brief. Written by the QA planner after reading the story's prompt file and the QA plan. Gives the tester exact instructions — tool, auth, seeds, what to test.

## Required Sections

### Tool

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Single line: tool name (web, curl, or script path)

Content:
- Which tool to use for this story's testing
- `web` for LiveView pages, `curl` or script path for controller/API routes


### Auth

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Exact commands or instructions the tester copies verbatim

Content:
- Login URL, credentials, headers — whatever the tool needs
- Reference auth scripts from the QA plan if applicable
- Tester should not need to figure out auth on their own


### Seeds

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Exact commands to run

Content:
- Seed script references (`mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`)
- Any story-specific seed commands beyond the base seeds
- Entity IDs or values the tester will need


### What To Test

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Bullet list of specific test scenarios

Content:
- Specific URLs to visit
- Interactions to perform (click, fill form, submit)
- Expected outcomes (what the tester should see)
- Map to acceptance criteria from the story


### Result Path

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Single line: file path

Content:
- Where the tester writes the result document


## Optional Sections

### Setup Notes

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Free-form paragraphs

Content:
- Additional context, prerequisites, known issues



## Findings and done signal

Every finding you uncover during execution gets filed via
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__create_issue` **as you find it** — not
written into a markdown file. Capture the title, severity, scope, and a
short description; the call returns an issue id. Hold those ids.

When you finish the session, call
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with the structured
scenarios payload **and** every issue id you filed:

    mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result(
      task_id: <task_id>,
      status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
      scenarios: [%{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."}, ...],
      issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue>]
    )

Discipline:

- **`status: "pass"`** with `issue_ids: []` is fine.
- **`status: "partial"` or `"fail"`** with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected
  by the tool**. A failure with no filed issue is a finding that just
  disappeared when your session ended — there's nowhere else for it to
  live. File the issues first, then submit.
- The bare `submit_qa_result` (without the `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__`
  prefix) does NOT resolve — use the fully-qualified name.
- Don't write findings into a result.md file. The harness doesn't read it.
  Screenshots and other evidence still belong on disk, but the canonical
  record is the DB attempt + linked issues.

# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM

## App Overview

Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).

## Tools Registry

### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)

Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.

### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)

Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)

Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.

## Seed Strategy

Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:

- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). Prints credentials and the login URL on completion. Run it after every `mix ecto.reset`, and before any browser session that needs a logged-in user. As domain contexts land (Clients, Scheduling, Quality, …), extend this script with clients/properties/plans rather than adding bash loops — one BEAM boot, all entities.
- `priv/repo/seeds.exs` — stock Phoenix seed file, currently empty; runs automatically during `mix ecto.setup`/`ecto.reset`.

## System Issues

### Port 4000 occupied by another dev app

Another BEAM app on this machine listens on 4000 (and answers `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with a `dev.codemyspec.com` issuer — it is NOT this app). Cleaner CRM's dev default was moved to **4100** (`config/runtime.exs`, `PORT` env still wins). If a probe of 4000 returns 200s, you are talking to the wrong app. Status: resolved (default port changed).

### `mix test` is rerouted to `mix agent_test`, which skips `ecto.create`

The harness rewrites `mix test`; on a fresh checkout the test DB may not exist and every test fails with `invalid_catalog_name`. Fix: `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate` once. Status: resolved on this machine, will recur on fresh clones.

## Notes

The `:api` pipeline exists but has no routes yet; when API/webhook endpoints land (Stripe webhooks, Twilio status callbacks, reminder confirm links), add curl rows with real headers here. Emails (magic link, invitations) are viewable at `http://127.0.0.1:4100/dev/mailbox` in dev — use it to extract tokens during browser QA. Integration verify scripts are `pending` until the engineer supplies credentials (see `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`).

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
4	  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
7	  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
8	  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
9	  """
10	
11	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
12	
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
14	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
17	  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
18	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}
19	
20	  ## Clocking in and out
21	
22	  @doc """
23	  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
24	  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
25	  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
26	  somewhere else.
27	  """
28	  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
29	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
31	         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
32	      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
33	    end
34	  end
35	
36	  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
37	  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
38	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
39	    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
40	      nil ->
41	        {:error, :not_clocked_in}
42	
43	      entry ->
44	        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
45	    end
46	  end
47	
48	  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
49	  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}
50	
51	  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
52	    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
53	      nil -> :ok
54	      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
55	      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
56	    end
57	  end
58	
59	  @doc """
60	  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
61	  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
62	  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
63	  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
64	  """
65	  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
66	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
67	    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))
68	
69	    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
70	    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
71	    |> Repo.insert()
72	  end
73	
74	  @doc """
75	  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
76	  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
77	  clock-out.
78	  """
79	  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
80	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
81	    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
82	         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
83	      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
84	    end
85	  end
86	
87	  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
88	    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
89	      {:ok, value} -> value
90	      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
91	    end
92	  end
93	
94	  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}
95	
96	  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
97	    case String.split(string, ":") do
98	      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
99	      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
100	    end
101	  end
102	
103	  # Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
104	  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
105	  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
106	  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
107	  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
108	  # forward to the next day instead.
109	  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
110	    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
111	
112	    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
113	      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
114	        {:ok, candidate}
115	      else
116	        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)
117	      end
118	    end
119	  end
120	
121	  ## Reading time entries
122	
123	  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
124	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
125	    TimeEntry
126	    |> where(
127	      [t],
128	      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
129	    )
130	    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
131	    |> limit(1)
132	    |> Repo.one()
133	  end
134	
135	  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
136	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
137	    TimeEntry
138	    |> where(
139	      [t],
140	      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
141	    )
142	    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
143	    |> limit(1)
144	    |> Repo.one()
145	  end
146	
147	  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
148	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
149	    TimeEntry
150	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
151	    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
152	    |> Repo.all()
153	  end
154	
155	  ## Earnings
156	
157	  @doc """
158	  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
159	  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
160	  """
161	  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
162	    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
163	  end
164	
165	  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
166	  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
167	    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
168	      nil -> nil
169	      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
170	    end
171	  end
172	
173	  ## Pay periods
174	
175	  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
176	  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
177	    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
178	    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
179	  end
180	
181	  @doc """
182	  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
183	  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
184	  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
185	  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
186	  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
187	  navigate first.
188	  """
189	  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
190	    TimeEntry
191	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
192	    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
193	    |> Repo.one()
194	    |> case do
195	      nil -> Date.utc_today()
196	      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
197	    end
198	    |> pay_period_for()
199	  end
200	
201	  @doc """
202	  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
203	  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
204	  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
205	  """
206	  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
207	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
208	    scope
209	    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
210	    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
211	    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
212	      job = hd(entries).job
213	      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)
214	
215	      %{
216	        job: job,
217	        cleaner: job.cleaner,
218	        entries: entries,
219	        cents: cents,
220	        # A job counts as unresolved whenever pay can't be computed yet
221	        # (a job missing its pay type entirely leaves `cents` `nil`
222	        # even once every entry is closed — that must block the same
223	        # way an open entry does, not silently price at $0) or whenever
224	        # an entry is still open — piece-rate pays a flat amount
225	        # regardless of entries, so `cents` alone wouldn't catch a
226	        # piece-rate job someone is still clocked in on.
227	        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))
228	      }
229	    end)
230	    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
231	  end
232	
233	  @doc """
234	  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
235	  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
236	  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
237	  """
238	  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
239	    scope
240	    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
241	    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
242	    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
243	      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
244	      {cleaner_id, total}
245	    end)
246	  end
247	
248	  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
249	    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
250	    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])
251	
252	    TimeEntry
253	    |> where(
254	      [t],
255	      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
256	    )
257	    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
258	    |> Repo.all()
259	  end
260	
261	  ## Payroll export
262	
263	  @doc """
264	  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
265	  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
266	  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
267	  """
268	  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
269	    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)
270	
271	    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
272	      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
273	    else
274	      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
275	    end
276	  end
277	
278	  ## Drive-time policy
279	
280	  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
281	  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
282	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
283	    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
284	  end
285	
286	  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)
287	
288	  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
289	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
290	    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
291	  end
292	
293	  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
294	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
295	    scope
296	    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
297	    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
298	    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
299	    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
300	  end
301	end
302

  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}

  ## Clocking in and out

  @doc """
  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
  somewhere else.
  """
  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
    end
  end

  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_clocked_in}

      entry ->
        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}

  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
      nil -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
  """
  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
  clock-out.
  """
  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> value
      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
    end
  end

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  # Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
  # forward to the next day instead.
  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)

    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
        {:ok, candidate}
      else
        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)
      end
    end
  end

  ## Reading time entries

  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Earnings

  @doc """
  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
  """
  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> nil
      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
    end
  end

  ## Pay periods

  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
  end

  @doc """
  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
  navigate first.
  """
  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      nil -> Date.utc_today()
      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
    end
    |> pay_period_for()
  end

  @doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job
      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: cents,
        # A job counts as unresolved whenever pay can't be computed yet
        # (a job missing its pay type entirely leaves `cents` `nil`
        # even once every entry is closed — that must block the same
        # way an open entry does, not silently price at $0) or whenever
        # an entry is still open — piece-rate pays a flat amount
        # regardless of entries, so `cents` alone wouldn't catch a
        # piece-rate job someone is still clocked in on.
        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

  @doc """
  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
  """
  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    scope
    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
      {cleaner_id, total}
    end)
  end

  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Payroll export

  @doc """
  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
  """
  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)

    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
    else
      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
    end
  end

  ## Drive-time policy

  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
  end

  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)

  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
  end

  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings do
  @moduledoc """
  Pure pay calculations — no scope, no `Repo`. Given a job and its
  time entries, this is the only place clocked time (or a fixed piece
  rate) turns into cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry

  @doc "Seconds between clock-in and clock-out. Only meaningful once resolved."
  def worked_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: in_at, clocked_out_at: out_at})
      when not is_nil(out_at) do
    DateTime.diff(out_at, in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed so far on a still-open entry."
  def elapsed_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_out_at: nil, clocked_in_at: in_at}) do
    DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc """
  Cents earned on a job given its (possibly empty) list of time
  entries: the flat piece rate regardless of time for a piece-rate job
  — shown even before the cleaner has started, since it doesn't
  depend on any entry existing — or the hourly rate times total
  resolved worked time. `nil` when an hourly job has no resolved
  entries yet, or a job carries neither pay type: there's nothing to
  compute pay from, and it must not be silently priced at $0.
  """
  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents}, _entries)
      when is_integer(cents) do
    cents
  end

  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: rate}, entries)
      when is_integer(rate) and is_list(entries) and entries != [] do
    if Enum.all?(entries, &TimeEntry.resolved?/1) do
      entries |> Enum.map(&worked_seconds/1) |> Enum.sum() |> hourly_cents(rate)
    end
  end

  def job_cents(_job, _entries), do: nil

  defp hourly_cents(seconds, rate_cents) do
    Decimal.new(rate_cents)
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.div(Decimal.new(seconds), Decimal.new(3600)))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.PayRate do
  @moduledoc """
  A cleaner's default pay basis and rate.

  A job's own `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job`) always take precedence when present —
  this is only the fallback a job-creation form would prefill from,
  one row per cleaner per account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          basis: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "pay_rates" do
    field :basis, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(cleaner_id basis rate_cents)a

  def changeset(pay_rate, attrs) do
    pay_rate
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required(@fields)
    |> validate_number(:rate_cents, greater_than: 0)
    |> unique_constraint([:account_id, :cleaner_id])
  end
end

input.title: No UI to set job pay type/rate — hourly pay, piece-rate pay, running totals, and CSV export are all unreachable
input.description:
Story 838 requires hourly pay (rate × hours), piece-rate pay (fixed amount), running pay-period totals, and CSV export. All four depend on a job's `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` fields (see CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2), but nothing in the web layer ever sets them.

Checked lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/job_form_component.ex: the `:new`, `:quick_new`, and `:edit` job forms only expose property, date, start/end time, price, and cleaner — no pay type or rate fields. Also checked CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.PayRate (a per-cleaner default rate/basis schema whose own moduledoc says a job's own fields "always take precedence... this is only the fallback a job-creation form would prefill from") — grepped the entire lib/cleaner_crm_web tree for `set_pay_rate`/`PayRate`/`pay_rate` and got zero hits. There is no settings page, no job-form field, nothing.

Consequence, verified live: every job in the dev DB has `pay_type = NULL`. I clocked a cleaner in and out of an assigned job via /field/jobs/:id (real time entry recorded: 2026-07-08 12:58:18 → 12:58:30). The owner's /timesheets page still shows "Pay period total: $0.00" and treats the job as unresolved, because `Earnings.job_cents/2` returns `nil` whenever `pay_type` is nil — regardless of how clean the clock-in/out was. There is no way, through any page in the app, for an owner to make a job's pay computable. Criteria 7125 (hourly), 7128 (piece rate), 7130 (running total), and 7134 (CSV export of a resolved period) cannot be exercised or demonstrated end-to-end — export is permanently disabled for every account in its current state.

input.title: Timesheet mislabels fully clocked-out jobs as "Missing clock-out"; Resolve button silently no-ops
input.description:
On /timesheets, CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive decides whether to show a job's pay or a "Missing clock-out" resolve form purely from `summary.unresolved?`, which is `is_nil(cents) or any entry not resolved` (see lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/timesheet_live.ex render + CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.list_job_time_summaries). Because `cents` is always nil (see linked pay-type issue), `unresolved?` is always true, so *every* job shows "Missing clock-out" and a resolve-clock-out form — even one with a complete, valid time entry.

Reproduced live: job 48ae34be-eb88-489b-9bd5-331476a9307b was clocked in at 12:58:18 and clocked out at 12:58:30 (verified via time_entries table, clocked_out_at populated). The timesheet still rendered it under "Missing clock-out" with a resolve-clock-out form (data-test="resolve-clock-out-form-48ae34be..."). Filling in a clock-out time and clicking Resolve produced no visible change and no error/flash — because TimesheetLive's "resolve_clock_out" handler calls `TimeTracking.open_time_entry_for_job/2`, which correctly returns `nil` (no open entry), and the handler's `nil -> socket` branch is a true no-op with zero feedback to the owner.

Separately, for the genuinely-open entry on job 51ef260f-90db-4357-9403-ea3574f9bac2, submitting a resolve did persist (clocked_out_at was set in the DB, confirmed via psql), but the timesheet UI continued to display that row as "Missing clock-out" with the resolve form still showing afterward — giving the owner no confirmation the fix worked and no way to tell a truly-open entry apart from a merely pay-type-less one. The template needs to distinguish "entry has no clock-out" from "job's pay can't be computed" instead of conflating both into one flag and one form.

scenarios.name: Cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job
scenarios.observation: Clocked in/out on /field/jobs/48ae34be-eb88-489b-9bd5-331476a9307b as qa-cleaner; time_entries row created with clocked_in_at 12:58:18 and clocked_out_at 12:58:30, confirmed via psql.

scenarios.name: Hourly job pays rate times worked hours
scenarios.observation: No UI anywhere sets a job's pay_type/hourly_rate_cents or a cleaner's default PayRate (zero references in lib/cleaner_crm_web). Every job has pay_type nil, so Earnings.job_cents/2 always returns nil. Unreachable via the app. Issue a9233027.

content.text:
Feature: Review photo proof and quality scorecards per job
  As a cleaning business owner, I want completed jobs to show checklist completion, before/after photos, and a quality scorecard per cleaner over time, so that I can verify work I can't inspect in person, coach consistently, and defend against complaints and chargebacks. (Research: verification is standard in STR tools but absent in residential/janitorial — the #3 synthesis gap — pain-points §1.5, §5)
  Rule: A job cannot be marked complete until every required checklist task is checked off or explicitly marked skipped with a reason.
    Scenario: Cleaner completes a job with a fully checked checklist
      Given a job with a room-by-room checklist of ten required tasks
      When the cleaner checks off all ten tasks and taps complete
      Then the job is marked complete with checklist completion recorded

    Scenario: Cleaner tries to complete with unchecked required tasks
      Given a job checklist with two required tasks still unchecked
      When the cleaner taps complete
      Then completion is blocked and the cleaner is prompted to check off or mark the remaining tasks skipped with a reason before the job can close

  Rule: Required before and after photos are captured per photo task and attached to the completed job with a timestamp.
    Scenario: Before and after photos attached with timestamps
      Given a checklist task that requires a before and an after photo of the kitchen
      When the cleaner captures both photos during the job
      Then both photos are attached to the completed job, each stamped with the time it was taken

  Rule: Each completed job produces a quality score derived from checklist completion and any owner quality review of the job.
    Scenario: Completed job gets a quality score
      Given a completed job with full checklist completion and all required photos
      When the owner reviews the job and rates it four out of five
      Then the job records a quality score combining checklist completion and the owner's rating

  Rule: A per-cleaner quality scorecard aggregates that cleaner's job scores over time so the owner can spot trends and coach.
    Scenario: Owner reviews a cleaner's scorecard over time
      Given a cleaner with twenty scored jobs over the last month
      When the owner opens that cleaner's quality scorecard
      Then the scorecard shows the average score and the trend across those jobs so the owner can coach on declining areas

  Rule: Completed-job proof — checklist state, photos, and timestamps — is retained and retrievable so the owner can defend against a complaint or chargeback.
    Scenario: Owner pulls up job proof to answer a chargeback
      Given a client disputes a charge claiming the job was not done
      When the owner opens the completed job from three weeks ago
      Then the owner sees the completed checklist, before and after photos, and timestamps to present as proof the work was performed

  Rule: Photos captured while the cleaner has no connection are queued on the device and uploaded automatically when connectivity returns.
    Scenario: Photo taken offline uploads when signal returns
      Given a cleaner in a basement with no cell signal captures the required after photos
      When the photo upload cannot reach the server
      Then the photos are queued on the device and upload automatically once the cleaner regains connectivity, without the cleaner having to retake them

<.button :if={is_nil(@checklist.completed_at)} data-test="mark-complete-button" phx-click="mark_complete" phx-target={@myself} class="mt-3" > Finish Job
""" end @impl true def update(assigns, socket) do {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:rooms, Quality.group_by_room(assigns.checklist)) |> assign(:progress, Quality.progress(assigns.checklist)) |> assign_new(:incomplete, fn -> [] end)} end @impl true def handle_event("mark_complete", _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope case Quality.complete_job(scope, socket.assigns.checklist) do {:ok, _completed} -> maybe_generate_invoice(scope, socket.assigns.job) send(self(), :job_completed) {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, [])} {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, incomplete)} end end def handle_event("skip", %{"item-id" => item_id}, socket) do item = Enum.find(socket.assigns.checklist.items, &(&1.id == item_id)) {:ok, _item} = Quality.skip_checklist_item(socket.assigns.current_scope, item, "Skipped by cleaner") send(self(), :checklist_changed) {:noreply, socket} end # Not every account has `CleanerCrm.Billing` wired to this hook yet # (see its moduledoc) — read defensively so this component never # needs to change again once it lands. defp maybe_generate_invoice(scope, job) do if Code.ensure_loaded?(Billing) and function_exported?(Billing, :generate_for_job, 2) do Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job) end end end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
4	  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
5	  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.
6	
7	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
8	  """
9	
10	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
11	
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
14	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
16	
17	  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
18	    Checklist,
19	    ChecklistItem,
20	    ChecklistTemplate,
21	    IncidentReport,
22	    Photo,
23	    Scorecard
24	  }
25	
26	  ## Checklist templates
27	
28	  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
29	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    ChecklistTemplate
31	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
32	    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
33	    |> preload(:property)
34	    |> Repo.all()
35	  end
36	
37	  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
38	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
39	    ChecklistTemplate
40	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
41	    |> preload(:property)
42	    |> Repo.get!(id)
43	  end
44	
45	  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
46	    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
47	  end
48	
49	  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
50	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
51	    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
52	    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
53	    |> Repo.insert()
54	  end
55	
56	  def update_checklist_template(
57	        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
58	        %ChecklistTemplate{} = template,
59	        attrs
60	      )
61	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
62	    template
63	    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
64	    |> Repo.update()
65	  end
66	
67	  ## Checklists
68	
69	  @doc """
70	  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
71	  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
72	  """
73	  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
74	    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
75	  end
76	
77	  @doc """
78	  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
79	  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
80	  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
81	
82	  Called with an empty `items` list and no explicit `template_id` in
83	  `opts`, this looks for a `ChecklistTemplate` on the job's property
84	  and instantiates from it instead of leaving the checklist empty.
85	  This is what lets `FieldLive.Job`'s lazy
86	  `create_checklist(scope, job, [])` — called the first time a
87	  cleaner opens a job with no checklist yet — pick up a real,
88	  room-by-room checklist once the office has built one for the
89	  property, without that caller needing to know templates exist.
90	  """
91	  def create_checklist(
92	        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
93	        %Job{id: job_id} = job,
94	        items,
95	        opts \\ []
96	      )
97	      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
98	    {items, opts} = apply_property_template(scope, job, items, opts)
99	
100	    Repo.transact(fn ->
101	      with {:ok, checklist} <-
102	             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
103	             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
104	             |> Repo.insert() do
105	        item_structs =
106	          items
107	          |> Enum.with_index()
108	          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
109	            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
110	          end)
111	
112	        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
113	      end
114	    end)
115	  end
116	
117	  defp apply_property_template(_scope, _job, items, opts) when items != [], do: {items, opts}
118	
119	  defp apply_property_template(scope, %Job{property_id: property_id}, [], opts) do
120	    cond do
121	      # `opts[:template_id]` is a keyword-list lookup (`Access.get/2`), which
122	      # isn't allowed in a guard — checked here in the body instead.
123	      not is_nil(opts[:template_id]) -> {[], opts}
124	      is_nil(property_id) -> {[], opts}
125	      true -> apply_found_template(scope, property_id, opts)
126	    end
127	  end
128	
129	  defp apply_found_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, property_id, opts) do
130	    case find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
131	      nil ->
132	        {[], opts}
133	
134	      template ->
135	        {ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), Keyword.put(opts, :template_id, template.id)}
136	    end
137	  end
138	
139	  defp find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
140	    ChecklistTemplate
141	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.property_id == ^property_id)
142	    |> order_by([t], desc: t.updated_at)
143	    |> limit(1)
144	    |> Repo.one()
145	  end
146	
147	  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
148	    params =
149	      attrs
150	      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
151	      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
152	      |> Map.put_new("position", position)
153	
154	    %ChecklistItem{}
155	    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
156	    |> Repo.insert!()
157	  end
158	
159	  @doc """
160	  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
161	  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
162	  """
163	  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
164	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
165	    Checklist
166	    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
167	    |> preload(items: :photos)
168	    |> Repo.one()
169	  end
170	
171	  @doc """
172	  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
173	  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
174	  grouped under `nil`.
175	  """
176	  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
177	    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
178	    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
179	    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
180	  end
181	
182	  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
183	  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}
184	
185	  @doc """
186	  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
187	  any prior skip.
188	  """
189	  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
190	    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()
191	  end
192	
193	  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item) do
194	    item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update()
195	  end
196	
197	  @doc "Marks a required item skipped instead of done, with a reason."
198	  def skip_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, reason) do
199	    item |> ChecklistItem.skip_changeset(reason) |> Repo.update()
200	  end
201	
202	  @doc """
203	  The required items still blocking completion: unchecked and not
204	  skipped. Empty means the checklist is ready to complete.
205	  """
206	  def incomplete_required_items(%Checklist{items: items}) do
207	    Enum.filter(items, &(&1.required and not &1.checked and not &1.skipped))
208	  end
209	
210	  @doc """
211	  Completes a job's checklist: refused with the still-incomplete
212	  required items when any remain; otherwise the checklist is stamped
213	  done, scored, and the job itself is marked completed.
214	  """
215	  def complete_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Checklist{} = checklist) do
216	    case incomplete_required_items(checklist) do
217	      [] -> do_complete_job(scope, checklist)
218	      incomplete -> {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}}
219	    end
220	  end
221	
222	  defp do_complete_job(scope, checklist) do
223	    Repo.transact(fn ->
224	      with {:ok, completed} <- mark_checklist_completed(checklist),
225	           {:ok, _job} <- mark_job_completed(scope, completed.job_id) do
226	        {:ok, completed}
227	      end
228	    end)
229	  end
230	
231	  defp mark_checklist_completed(checklist) do
232	    checklist
233	    |> Checklist.changeset(%{
234	      completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
235	      quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
236	    })
237	    |> Repo.update()
238	  end
239	
240	  defp mark_job_completed(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, job_id) do
241	    job = Job |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id) |> Repo.get!(job_id)
242	
243	    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :completed}) |> Repo.update() do
244	      Recorder.record(
245	        scope,
246	        "job_completed",
247	        "Job",
248	        updated.id,
249	        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
250	        %{"status" => "completed"}
251	      )
252	
253	      {:ok, updated}
254	    end
255	  end
256	
257	  @doc """
258	  Records the owner's 1-5 quality rating for a job, recomputing the
259	  checklist's combined quality score.
260	  """
261	  def rate_job(%Scope{}, %Checklist{} = checklist, rating) do
262	    rated = %{checklist | owner_rating: rating}
263	
264	    checklist
265	    |> Checklist.changeset(%{owner_rating: rating, quality_score: Scorecard.score(rated)})
266	    |> Repo.update()
267	  end
268	
269	  @doc """
270	  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
271	  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
272	  proof of work directly (see
273	  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
274	  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
275	  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
276	  """
277	  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
278	      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
279	    Repo.transact(fn ->
280	      with {:ok, checklist} <-
281	             create_checklist(
282	               scope,
283	               job,
284	               Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))
285	             ) do
286	        checked_items =
287	          checklist.items
288	          |> Enum.zip(items)
289	          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)
290	
291	        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}
292	
293	        checklist
294	        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
295	          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
296	          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
297	        })
298	        |> Repo.update()
299	      end
300	    end)
301	  end
302	
303	  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{
304	         before_photo: before_photo,
305	         after_photo: after_photo
306	       }) do
307	    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
308	    before = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
309	    aftr = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
310	    %{checked | photos: [before, aftr]}
311	  end
312	
313	  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
314	    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
315	    |> Photo.changeset(%{
316	      checklist_item_id: item.id,
317	      kind: kind,
318	      upload_state: :uploaded,
319	      storage_key: storage_key,
320	      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
321	    })
322	    |> Repo.insert!()
323	  end
324	
325	  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."
326	  def attach_photo(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, attrs)
327	      when not is_nil(account_id) and kind in [:before, :after] do
328	    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
329	    |> Photo.changeset(Map.merge(%{checklist_item_id: item.id, kind: kind}, attrs))
330	    |> Repo.insert()
331	  end
332	
333	  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
334	  def complete_photo_upload(%Scope{}, %Photo{} = photo, storage_key) do
335	    photo |> Photo.uploaded_changeset(storage_key) |> Repo.update()
336	  end
337	
338	  ## Incident reports
339	
340	  @doc """
341	  Files an incident report for a job. `attrs` needs `:type`
342	  (`"damage"`, `"missing_item"`, or `"unsafe_condition"`) and
343	  `:description`; a `:photo` (the same attrs `attach_photo/4` takes)
344	  is required unless `:type` is `"unsafe_condition"`. The cleaner and
345	  filing time are always the caller's and now — never accepted from
346	  `attrs` — and nothing about a filed report can change afterward.
347	  """
348	  def file_incident_report(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id, user: user}, %Job{} = job, attrs)
349	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
350	    {photo_attrs, report_attrs} = attrs |> stringify_keys() |> Map.pop("photo")
351	
352	    Repo.transact(fn ->
353	      with {:ok, report} <-
354	             %IncidentReport{account_id: account_id}
355	             |> IncidentReport.changeset(
356	               Map.merge(report_attrs, %{
357	                 "job_id" => job.id,
358	                 "cleaner_id" => user && user.id,
359	                 "filed_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
360	               }),
361	               not is_nil(photo_attrs)
362	             )
363	             |> Repo.insert() do
364	        photo = photo_attrs && insert_incident_photo!(account_id, report, photo_attrs)
365	        {:ok, %{report | photos: Enum.filter([photo], & &1)}}
366	      end
367	    end)
368	  end
369	
370	  defp stringify_keys(attrs), do: Map.new(attrs, fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
371	
372	  defp insert_incident_photo!(account_id, %IncidentReport{} = report, photo_attrs) do
373	    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
374	    |> Photo.changeset(
375	      Map.merge(stringify_keys(photo_attrs), %{
376	        "incident_report_id" => report.id,
377	        "kind" => "incident",
378	        "upload_state" => "uploaded",
379	        "captured_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
380	      })
381	    )
382	    |> Repo.insert!()
383	  end
384	
385	  @doc """
386	  Lists an account's incident reports, most recently filed first,
387	  with job (and its client), cleaner, and photos preloaded.
388	  """
389	  def list_incident_reports(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
390	    IncidentReport
391	    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
392	    |> order_by([r], desc: r.filed_at)
393	    |> preload([:cleaner, :photos, job: [:client, :property]])

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> preload(:property)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(:property)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def update_checklist_template(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %ChecklistTemplate{} = template,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    template
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Checklists

  @doc """
  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
  """
  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.

  Called with an empty `items` list and no explicit `template_id` in
  `opts`, this looks for a `ChecklistTemplate` on the job's property
  and instantiates from it instead of leaving the checklist empty.
  This is what lets `FieldLive.Job`'s lazy
  `create_checklist(scope, job, [])` — called the first time a
  cleaner opens a job with no checklist yet — pick up a real,
  room-by-room checklist once the office has built one for the
  property, without that caller needing to know templates exist.
  """
  def create_checklist(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Job{id: job_id} = job,
        items,
        opts \\ []
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    {items, opts} = apply_property_template(scope, job, items, opts)

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
          end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp apply_property_template(_scope, _job, items, opts) when items != [], do: {items, opts}

  defp apply_property_template(scope, %Job{property_id: property_id}, [], opts) do
    cond do
      # `opts[:template_id]` is a keyword-list lookup (`Access.get/2`), which
      # isn't allowed in a guard — checked here in the body instead.
      not is_nil(opts[:template_id]) -> {[], opts}
      is_nil(property_id) -> {[], opts}
      true -> apply_found_template(scope, property_id, opts)
    end
  end

  defp apply_found_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, property_id, opts) do
    case find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
      nil ->
        {[], opts}

      template ->
        {ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), Keyword.put(opts, :template_id, template.id)}
    end
  end

  defp find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.property_id == ^property_id)
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.updated_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
  """
  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
    |> preload(items: :photos)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc """
  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
  grouped under `nil`.
  """
  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
  end

  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}

  @doc """
  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
  any prior skip.
  """
  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped instead of done, with a reason."
  def skip_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, reason) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.skip_changeset(reason) |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  The required items still blocking completion: unchecked and not
  skipped. Empty means the checklist is ready to complete.
  """
  def incomplete_required_items(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    Enum.filter(items, &(&1.required and not &1.checked and not &1.skipped))
  end

  @doc """
  Completes a job's checklist: refused with the still-incomplete
  required items when any remain; otherwise the checklist is stamped
  done, scored, and the job itself is marked completed.
  """
  def complete_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Checklist{} = checklist) do
    case incomplete_required_items(checklist) do
      [] -> do_complete_job(scope, checklist)
      incomplete -> {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}}
    end
  end

  defp do_complete_job(scope, checklist) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, completed} <- mark_checklist_completed(checklist),
           {:ok, _job} <- mark_job_completed(scope, completed.job_id) do
        {:ok, completed}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp mark_checklist_completed(checklist) do
    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{
      completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
    })
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp mark_job_completed(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, job_id) do
    job = Job |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id) |> Repo.get!(job_id)

    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :completed}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_completed",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "completed"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Records the owner's 1-5 quality rating for a job, recomputing the
  checklist's combined quality score.
  """
  def rate_job(%Scope{}, %Checklist{} = checklist, rating) do
    rated = %{checklist | owner_rating: rating}

    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{owner_rating: rating, quality_score: Scorecard.score(rated)})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
  proof of work directly (see
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
  """
  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             create_checklist(
               scope,
               job,
               Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))
             ) do
        checked_items =
          checklist.items
          |> Enum.zip(items)
          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)

        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}

        checklist
        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
        })
        |> Repo.update()
      end
    end)
  end

  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{
         before_photo: before_photo,
         after_photo: after_photo
       }) do
    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
    before = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
    aftr = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
    %{checked | photos: [before, aftr]}
  end

  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(%{
      checklist_item_id: item.id,
      kind: kind,
      upload_state: :uploaded,
      storage_key: storage_key,
      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."
  def attach_photo(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and kind in [:before, :after] do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(Map.merge(%{checklist_item_id: item.id, kind: kind}, attrs))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
  def complete_photo_upload(%Scope{}, %Photo{} = photo, storage_key) do
    photo |> Photo.uploaded_changeset(storage_key) |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Incident reports

  @doc """
  Files an incident report for a job. `attrs` needs `:type`
  (`"damage"`, `"missing_item"`, or `"unsafe_condition"`) and
  `:description`; a `:photo` (the same attrs `attach_photo/4` takes)
  is required unless `:type` is `"unsafe_condition"`. The cleaner and
  filing time are always the caller's and now — never accepted from
  `attrs` — and nothing about a filed report can change afterward.
  """
  def file_incident_report(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id, user: user}, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    {photo_attrs, report_attrs} = attrs |> stringify_keys() |> Map.pop("photo")

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, report} <-
             %IncidentReport{account_id: account_id}
             |> IncidentReport.changeset(
               Map.merge(report_attrs, %{
                 "job_id" => job.id,
                 "cleaner_id" => user && user.id,
                 "filed_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
               }),
               not is_nil(photo_attrs)
             )
             |> Repo.insert() do
        photo = photo_attrs && insert_incident_photo!(account_id, report, photo_attrs)
        {:ok, %{report | photos: Enum.filter([photo], & &1)}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp stringify_keys(attrs), do: Map.new(attrs, fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)

  defp insert_incident_photo!(account_id, %IncidentReport{} = report, photo_attrs) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(
      Map.merge(stringify_keys(photo_attrs), %{
        "incident_report_id" => report.id,
        "kind" => "incident",
        "upload_state" => "uploaded",
        "captured_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
      })
    )
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists an account's incident reports, most recently filed first,
  with job (and its client), cleaner, and photos preloaded.
  """
  def list_incident_reports(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    IncidentReport
    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([r], desc: r.filed_at)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :photos, job: [:client, :property]])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Scorecards

  @doc """
  The cleaner's average quality score and trend across their
  completed jobs, oldest first (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`).
  """
  def cleaner_scorecard(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> join(:inner, [c], j in Job, on: j.id == c.job_id)
    |> where(
      [c, j],
      c.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        not is_nil(c.completed_at)
    )
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.completed_at)
    |> select([c], c.quality_score)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
    |> Scorecard.aggregate()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo do
  @moduledoc """
  A stored before/after (checklist proof) or incident photo, with
  offline-tolerant upload state.

  Per the file-storage ADR, uploads land in S3-compatible object
  storage via presigned URLs from the phone — a `Photo` row exists
  from the moment the cleaner picks the file (`:pending`, no
  `storage_key` yet) so a dropped connection just leaves it pending
  until the retry lands (`:uploaded`, `storage_key` set).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type kind :: :before | :after | :incident
  @type upload_state :: :pending | :uploaded

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          checklist_item_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          incident_report_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          kind: kind() | nil,
          upload_state: upload_state(),
          storage_key: String.t() | nil,
          captured_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "photos" do
    field :kind, Ecto.Enum, values: [:before, :after, :incident]
    field :upload_state, Ecto.Enum, values: [:pending, :uploaded], default: :pending
    field :storage_key, :string
    field :captured_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :checklist_item, CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :incident_report, CleanerCrm.Quality.IncidentReport, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(photo, attrs) do
    photo
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :account_id,
      :checklist_item_id,
      :incident_report_id,
      :kind,
      :upload_state,
      :storage_key,
      :captured_at
    ])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :kind])
    |> validate_one_owner()
  end

  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
  def uploaded_changeset(photo, storage_key) do
    change(photo, upload_state: :uploaded, storage_key: storage_key)
  end

  defp validate_one_owner(changeset) do
    case {get_field(changeset, :checklist_item_id), get_field(changeset, :incident_report_id)} do
      {nil, nil} ->
        add_error(changeset, :checklist_item_id, "or incident_report_id is required")

      {_id, nil} ->
        changeset

      {nil, _id} ->
        changeset

      {_checklist_item_id, _incident_report_id} ->
        add_error(changeset, :checklist_item_id, "and incident_report_id cannot both be set")
    end
  end
end
