defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem do
  @moduledoc """
  A single room/task line on a job's checklist: its required flag,
  checked/skipped completion state, and the before/after photos
  attached to it as proof.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          checklist_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          room: String.t() | nil,
          task: String.t() | nil,
          required: boolean(),
          checked: boolean(),
          checked_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          skipped: boolean(),
          skip_reason: String.t() | nil,
          position: integer(),
          photos: [Photo.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "checklist_items" do
    field :room, :string
    field :task, :string
    field :required, :boolean, default: true
    field :checked, :boolean, default: false
    field :checked_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :skipped, :boolean, default: false
    field :skip_reason, :string
    field :position, :integer, default: 0

    belongs_to :checklist, CleanerCrm.Quality.Checklist, type: :binary_id
    has_many :photos, Photo

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(item, attrs) do
    item
    |> cast(attrs, [:checklist_id, :room, :task, :required, :position])
    |> validate_required([:checklist_id, :task])
  end

  @doc "Checks the item off, stamping when, and clears any prior skip."
  def check_changeset(item) do
    change(item, checked: true, checked_at: DateTime.utc_now(), skipped: false, skip_reason: nil)
  end

  @doc "Reverts a checked item back to unchecked."
  def uncheck_changeset(item) do
    change(item, checked: false, checked_at: nil)
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped, with a reason, instead of done."
  def skip_changeset(item, reason) do
    item
    |> change(skipped: true, skip_reason: reason, checked: false, checked_at: nil)
    |> validate_required([:skip_reason])
  end
end

content.text: I have solid findings. Let me file the three issues for story 839.

input.title: Skip-with-reason never captures or displays a real reason — always hardcoded "Skipped by cleaner"
input.description:
Criterion 7163 expects a required task to be "mark[ed] skipped with a reason" — implying the cleaner supplies a real, meaningful reason (e.g. "client's closet was locked") that the owner can later see, especially valuable for defending a chargeback (this story's stated purpose).

In practice: lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/checklist_component.ex's `handle_event("skip", %{"item-id" => item_id}, socket)` calls `Quality.skip_checklist_item(socket.assigns.current_scope, item, "Skipped by cleaner")` with a literal hardcoded string — there is no modal, prompt, or text input anywhere in the "Skip with reason" button's flow for the cleaner to type an actual reason, despite `ChecklistItem.skip_reason` existing as a real schema field built for exactly this.

Compounding it: even if a real reason were ever captured, the owner's review page (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/quality_live/review.ex) never renders `item.skip_reason` at all — it only shows a generic "Skipped" badge with no reason text anywhere in the UI. So today, every skip in the system is indistinguishable from every other, and the owner has no way to see why a task was skipped even by inspecting the completed job.

Reproduced live: created job bb40913a-e5b1-44f2-af4e-fa46520781d8 (property 836 Card St, template with 2 required tasks), confirmed the checklist item's skip path via code path only (didn't need to click through — the handler takes no reason param from the client at all).

input.title: "Still needed before this job is done" banner doesn't clear after required tasks are checked off
input.description:
On /field/jobs/:id, after clicking "Finish Job" with unchecked required tasks, the checklist shows an "incomplete required tasks" warning listing them. Reproduced on job bb40913a-e5b1-44f2-af4e-fa46520781d8: clicked Finish Job with 0/3 checked, saw the warning listing "Wipe countertops" and "Scrub tub". Then checked off both of those required items (with before/after photos attached) — the warning banner continued to display both tasks as still-needed, unchanged, even though the checklist progress counter correctly updated to "2 of 3".

Clicking "Finish Job" again did succeed immediately (job marked Complete), so this is cosmetic rather than a functional block — but it's a real, reproducible display bug: `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`'s `:incomplete` assign is only set inside the `mark_complete` event handler on failure, and nothing recomputes or clears it when a `:checklist_changed` update comes in from checking/unchecking an item. A cleaner who checks off the last required task and doesn't immediately re-click Finish Job has no way to tell, from the banner alone, that they're actually done — and might be misled into clicking "Skip with reason" on a task they already completed.

input.title: No offline-tolerant photo capture exists — contradicts Photo schema's own documented design
input.description:
Criterion 7176 requires photos captured with no signal to queue on-device and upload automatically once connectivity returns, without a retake. `CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo`'s own moduledoc describes exactly this: "uploads land in S3-compatible object storage via presigned URLs from the phone — a Photo row exists from the moment the cleaner picks the file (:pending, no storage_key yet) so a dropped connection just leaves it pending until the retry lands."

The actual implementation doesn't match that design. lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/checklist_item_component.ex uses a standard Phoenix LiveView `live_file_input` with `auto_upload: true`; `Quality.attach_photo/4` (which inserts the `Photo` row) is only called from inside `handle_progress` once `entry.done?` is true — meaning no `:pending` Photo row is ever created at file-selection time as the moduledoc describes, and the whole upload is a synchronous round-trip over the live socket rather than a presigned direct-to-storage upload from the phone.

Grepped the entire lib/ and assets/ trees for offline/queue/service-worker/indexedDB/localStorage handling: nothing exists client-side to persist a picked photo across a dropped connection. A Phoenix LiveView socket disconnect (e.g., a cleaner losing cell signal in a basement) aborts any in-flight upload; when the LiveView remounts on reconnect, `mount/3` re-runs fresh and the previously-picked file selection is gone — there is no automatic resume or retry. This couldn't be exercised directly through the browser (no network-throttling control available in this session), but the code path leaves no mechanism for the described behavior to occur, so criterion 7176 is very likely unimplemented rather than just untested.

content.text:
Feature: See an audit trail of schedule and record changes
  As a cleaning business owner, I want an audit trail showing who changed what (jobs, assignments, client records, prices) and when, so that I can untangle scheduling mistakes and hold my office team accountable. (Research: direct MaidCentral user wish — "an audit trail feature to track who makes changes" — pain-points §4)
  Rule: Every create, update, or delete of an audited record — job, assignment, client record, or price — records who made the change, what changed, and when.
    Scenario: Office staff reschedules a job and it is logged
      Given office staffer Dana is signed in
      When Dana moves a job from Tuesday 9:00 to Wednesday 1:00
      Then an audit entry records that Dana rescheduled that job, the old and new times, and the timestamp of the change

  Rule: Each audit entry captures the before and after values of the fields that changed.
    Scenario: Price change records old and new value
      Given a client's recurring job is priced at $120
      When Dana changes the price to $140
      Then the audit entry shows the price field changed from $120 to $140 and leaves other unchanged fields out of the entry

  Rule: The audit log is append-only per company — entries cannot be edited or deleted by anyone, including the owner.
    Scenario: Nobody can alter or delete an audit entry
      Given an audit entry recording a disputed schedule change
      When the owner or any user attempts to edit or delete that entry
      Then the system provides no way to modify or remove it and the entry remains intact

  Rule: A change made by an automated or system process is attributed to the system so that every audit entry has a named actor.
    Scenario: Automated recurring job generation is attributed to the system
      Given a recurring plan that automatically generates next week's jobs overnight
      When the system creates those jobs with no human involved
      Then each resulting audit entry names the system as the actor rather than showing a blank author

  Rule: The owner can filter the audit trail by user, record type, specific record, and date range to untangle a change.
    Scenario: Owner filters the trail to find who moved a job
      Given a client complains their Friday job vanished from the schedule
      When the owner filters the audit trail to that job over the past week
      Then the owner sees the entry showing which user deleted or moved the job and when

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Free-form paragraphs

Content:
- Additional context, prerequisites, known issues



## Findings and done signal

Every finding you uncover during execution gets filed via
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__create_issue` **as you find it** — not
written into a markdown file. Capture the title, severity, scope, and a
short description; the call returns an issue id. Hold those ids.

When you finish the session, call
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with the structured
scenarios payload **and** every issue id you filed:

    mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result(
      task_id: <task_id>,
      status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
      scenarios: [%{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."}, ...],
      issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue>]
    )

Discipline:

- **`status: "pass"`** with `issue_ids: []` is fine.
- **`status: "partial"` or `"fail"`** with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected
  by the tool**. A failure with no filed issue is a finding that just
  disappeared when your session ended — there's nowhere else for it to
  live. File the issues first, then submit.
- The bare `submit_qa_result` (without the `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__`
  prefix) does NOT resolve — use the fully-qualified name.
- Don't write findings into a result.md file. The harness doesn't read it.
  Screenshots and other evidence still belong on disk, but the canonical
  record is the DB attempt + linked issues.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit do
  @moduledoc """
  Read-side of the append-only audit trail: filtered listing of the
  entries `CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder` appends.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Lists the account's audit entries, most recent first, optionally
  narrowed by a filter map (string or atom keys):

  - `:subject_id` — exact match against the subject the entry is about
  - `:date_from` — inclusive lower bound (a `Date` or an ISO 8601 string)
  - `:date_to` — inclusive upper bound (a `Date` or an ISO 8601 string)

  A blank or absent value for any key leaves that filter off.
  """
  def list_entries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, filters \\ %{})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where([e], e.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> filter_by_subject(fetch(filters, :subject_id))
    |> filter_by_date_from(fetch(filters, :date_from))
    |> filter_by_date_to(fetch(filters, :date_to))
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp fetch(filters, key), do: Map.get(filters, key) || Map.get(filters, to_string(key))

  defp filter_by_subject(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_subject(query, subject_id),
    do: where(query, [e], e.subject_id == ^subject_id)

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, %Date{} = date),
    do: where(query, [e], e.inserted_at >= ^start_of_day(date))

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, date_string) when is_binary(date_string),
    do: filter_by_date_from(query, Date.from_iso8601!(date_string))

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, %Date{} = date),
    do: where(query, [e], e.inserted_at < ^start_of_day(Date.add(date, 1)))

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, date_string) when is_binary(date_string),
    do: filter_by_date_to(query, Date.from_iso8601!(date_string))

  defp start_of_day(date), do: DateTime.new!(date, ~T[00:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder do
  @moduledoc """
  API other contexts call to append audit trail entries.

  Callers pass the acting scope, an action string, the subject being
  changed, and old/new value maps. Nothing here ever updates or deletes
  a row — this module only ever inserts.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Records an audit entry attributed to the scope's current user.
  """
  def record(
        %Scope{} = scope,
        action,
        subject_type,
        subject_id,
        old_value \\ %{},
        new_value \\ %{}
      )
      when is_binary(action) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    insert(scope, %{system: false, actor_id: scope.user && scope.user.id}, action, subject_type,
      subject_id: subject_id,
      old_value: old_value,
      new_value: new_value
    )
  end

  @doc """
  Records an audit entry attributed to the system rather than a human
  actor — for automated processes such as recurring job materialization.
  """
  def record_system(
        %Scope{} = scope,
        action,
        subject_type,
        subject_id,
        old_value \\ %{},
        new_value \\ %{}
      )
      when is_binary(action) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    insert(scope, %{system: true, actor_id: nil}, action, subject_type,
      subject_id: subject_id,
      old_value: old_value,
      new_value: new_value
    )
  end

  defp insert(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, actor_attrs, action, subject_type, rest)
       when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AuditEntry{}
    |> AuditEntry.changeset(
      Map.merge(actor_attrs, %{
        account_id: account_id,
        action: action,
        subject_type: subject_type,
        subject_id: rest[:subject_id],
        old_value: rest[:old_value],
        new_value: rest[:new_value]
      })
    )
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries for a subject, most recent first.
  """
  def list_for_subject(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, subject_type, subject_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where(
      [e],
      e.account_id == ^account_id and e.subject_type == ^subject_type and
        e.subject_id == ^subject_id
    )
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry do
  @moduledoc """
  An immutable record of actor, action, subject, and old/new values.

  Append-only: no update or delete function is exposed anywhere in the
  codebase, and the `audit_entries` table itself has DB rules blocking
  UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth (see the migration that created it).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          actor_id: integer() | nil,
          system: boolean(),
          action: String.t() | nil,
          subject_type: String.t() | nil,
          subject_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          old_value: map(),
          new_value: map(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "audit_entries" do
    field :system, :boolean, default: false
    field :action, :string
    field :subject_type, :string
    field :subject_id, Ecto.UUID
    field :old_value, :map, default: %{}
    field :new_value, :map, default: %{}

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :actor, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
  end

  def changeset(entry, attrs) do
    entry
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :account_id,
      :actor_id,
      :system,
      :action,
      :subject_type,
      :subject_id,
      :old_value,
      :new_value
    ])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :action, :subject_type, :subject_id])
  end
end

  defp job_created_values(job) do

  @doc """

      when not is_nil(account_id) do

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])

  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """

      when not is_nil(account_id) do

             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,

             exclude_job_id: job.id

## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope

input.title: Audit trail can only be filtered by Subject ID and date range — no filter by user or record type
input.description:
Criterion 7201 promises the owner can "filter the audit trail by user, record type, specific record, and date range." The actual implementation supports only 2 of those 4 dimensions.

`CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive`'s filter form (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/audit_live.ex) renders exactly three inputs: Subject ID (text), From (date), To (date) — no actor/user picker and no record-type (Job/Client/Property/...) selector anywhere. The backing query, `CleanerCrm.Audit.list_entries/2` (lib/cleaner_crm/audit.ex), only implements `filter_by_subject/2` (exact `subject_id` match), `filter_by_date_from/2`, and `filter_by_date_to/2` — there is no filter clause for `actor_id`/`system` or `subject_type` at all, despite both columns existing and being indexed on the `audit_entries` table.

This directly undermines the story's own worked scenario: "a client complains their Friday job vanished... the owner filters the audit trail to that job over the past week." To use the existing Subject ID filter the owner would first need to already know the job's raw UUID — there's no job/client picker, no "show me everything Dana changed" option, and no way to narrow to just Client or just Job entries. The date-range half of the criterion works fine; the user and record-type half is entirely missing.

scenarios.name: Office staff reschedules a job and it is logged
scenarios.observation: Code review only: Scheduling.update_job/3 -> record_job_updated correctly labels the action job_rescheduled and snapshots old/new scheduled_date/start_time/end_time when changed. Could not click through the schedule board's Edit form live -- mid-session /assets/css/app.css and /assets/js/app.js started 404ing (confirmed via curl, persisted through a full browser restart), killing all LiveView interactivity app-wide. scenarios.name: Price change records old and new value
scenarios.observation: Same situation as the reschedule scenario: code (record_job_updated, @audited_update_fields, audit_snapshot) correctly restricts the entry to only the agreed_price_cents field when just price changes, leaving other fields out. Not live-verified due to the mid-session asset outage; no historical job_price_changed entries exist in the DB.

scenarios.name: Nobody can alter or delete an audit entry
scenarios.observation: Verified via code: CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder only ever inserts (no update/delete function exists anywhere), AuditLive's render has no edit/delete affordance for any entry, and the migration (20260707180010_create_audit_entries_table.exs) adds Postgres RULEs audit_entries_no_update/audit_entries_no_delete that both DO INSTEAD NOTHING -- defense in depth even against a raw SQL statement. scenarios.observation: The audit filter form and CleanerCrm.Audit.list_entries/2 only support Subject ID (exact UUID match) and a date range -- there is no filter by user/actor and no filter by record type, despite the criterion promising all four dimensions. scenarios.observation: Created a recurring plan via /schedule/plans/new (12 Cedar Ct, weekly, start 2026-07-13, 3 visits) before the asset outage hit; all 3 generated jobs got audit_entries with system=true, actor_id=null, action=job_created, and /audit correctly rendered them as 'System created Alex Rivera ... 2026-07-08 13:15' rather than a blank actor.

**Story 838 (time & pay tracking) — FAIL.** Clock-in/out and unassigned-job rejection both work. **Story 840 (audit trail) — PARTIAL.** System-attributed audit entries for recurring job generation and append-only enforcement (Postgres RULEs blocking UPDATE/DELETE) both confirmed. The filter form only supports Subject ID and date range — no filter by user or record type as the criterion requires (1 issue filed). # QA Story 838: Track time and per-job pay in one system

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning business owner, I want cleaner clock-in/out and per-job pay (hourly or piece-rate) tracked in the same system as scheduling, with a payroll-ready export, so that I stop running a parallel time-tracking system and pay disputes disappear. (Research: owners maintain separate clock-in systems; no payroll integration is a named ZenMaid gap — pain-points §1.3, §4)

## Acceptance criteria

- Cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job
- Cleaner tries to clock in on a job not assigned to them
- Hourly job pays rate times worked hours
- Per-job piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time
- Running pay-period total builds as jobs complete
- Owner exports a completed pay period to CSV
- Cleaner forgets to clock out
- Export blocked while an unresolved time entry remains

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create a single job, or assign/reassign a cleaner to an existing one. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|-----------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :assign` | yes | `:new` renders the full job form; `:assign` renders just the cleaner picker for an existing job | | job | `Job.t()` | yes | blank `%Job{}` for `:new`, loaded job for `:assign` | On a successful `:new` save, navigates itself to the new job's show page. On a successful `:assign`, sends `{__MODULE__, {:saved, job}}` to the parent instead (there's nowhere further to go — the parent just refreshes). Two more actions embed this same component inline on `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` (the board) rather than standalone: `:quick_new` (the board's own "New Job" button — same form as `:new`, but sends `{__MODULE__, {:job_created, job}}` to the parent instead of navigating away, since the point is to see the new job's brief on the board itself) and `:edit` (the board's per-job "Edit" button — reschedule and/or price change via `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.update_job/3`, sending `{__MODULE__, {:job_updated, job}}`). Neither touches `cleaner_id` — (re)assignment stays on the conflict-checked `:assign` path. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component import Ecto.Query, warn: false alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property alias CleanerCrm.Repo alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job @impl true def render(%{action: :assign} = assigns) do ~H"""
<.header>Assign Cleaner

{@conflict_error}

<.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="assignment-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:cleaner_id]} type="select" label="Cleaner" prompt="Unassigned" options={cleaner_options(@cleaners)} />
<.button phx-disable-with="Assigning...">Assign Cleaner
""" end def render(%{action: :edit} = assigns) do ~H"""
<.header>Edit Job <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="job-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input type="date" name="job[date]" id={@form[:scheduled_date].id} label="Date" value={@form[:scheduled_date].value} errors={field_errors(@form[:scheduled_date])} /> <.input field={@form[:start_time]} type="time" label="Start Time" /> <.input field={@form[:end_time]} type="time" label="End Time" /> <.input field={@form[:agreed_price]} type="number" step="0.01" label="Price ($)" /> <.pay_rate_inputs form={@form} pay_rate_input={@pay_rate_input} />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Changes
""" end def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header>New Job <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="job-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:property_id]} type="select" label="Property" prompt="Select a property" options={property_options(@properties)} /> <.input type="date" name="job[date]" id={@form[:scheduled_date].id} label="Date" value={@form[:scheduled_date].value} errors={field_errors(@form[:scheduled_date])} /> <.input field={@form[:start_time]} type="time" label="Start Time" /> <.input field={@form[:end_time]} type="time" label="End Time" /> <.input field={@form[:agreed_price]} type="number" step="0.01" label="Price ($)" /> <.pay_rate_inputs form={@form} pay_rate_input={@pay_rate_input} /> <.input field={@form[:cleaner_id]} type="select" label="Cleaner" prompt="Unassigned" options={cleaner_options(@cleaners)} />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Job
""" end # The pay-type select and its matching rate input, shared by the # `:new`/`:quick_new` and `:edit` forms (`:assign` never touches # pay). Only one rate input renders at a time, chosen by the form's # current `pay_type` — its raw dollar text lives in `@pay_rate_input` # rather than on the changeset, since `hourly_rate`/`piece_rate` # aren't real fields on `Job` (only the `_cents` columns are); the # dollar amount is converted to cents in `split_pay_params/1` before # it ever reaches the changeset. defp pay_rate_inputs(assigns) do ~H""" <.input field={@form[:pay_type]} type="select" label="Cleaner pay type" prompt="Not set" options={pay_type_options()} /> <.input :if={pay_type_value(@form) == "hourly"} type="number" step="0.01" min="0" name="job[hourly_rate]" id={@form[:hourly_rate_cents].id} label="Hourly rate ($)" value={@pay_rate_input} errors={field_errors(@form[:hourly_rate_cents])} /> <.input :if={pay_type_value(@form) == "piece_rate"} type="number" step="0.01" min="0" name="job[piece_rate]" id={@form[:piece_rate_cents].id} label="Piece rate ($)" value={@pay_rate_input} errors={field_errors(@form[:piece_rate_cents])} /> """ end @impl true def update(%{job: job, action: action} = assigns, socket) do {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:conflict_error, nil) |> assign(:properties, list_properties(assigns.current_scope)) |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(assigns.current_scope)) |> assign(:pay_rate_input, initial_pay_rate_input(job)) |> assign(:form, build_form(assigns.current_scope, job, action))} end defp build_form(scope, job, action) when action in [:new, :quick_new], do: to_form(Scheduling.change_job(scope, job), as: :job) defp build_form(scope, job, :edit), do: to_form(Scheduling.change_job(scope, with_display_price(job)), as: :job) defp build_form(scope, job, :assign), do: to_form(Scheduling.change_job(scope, job), as: :assignment) # `agreed_price` is virtual and isn't derived from the persisted # `agreed_price_cents` on load, so the edit form would otherwise # show a blank price for a job that already has one. defp with_display_price(%Job{agreed_price_cents: nil} = job), do: job defp with_display_price(%Job{agreed_price_cents: cents} = job), do: %{job | agreed_price: cents |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100))} @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"job" => params}, socket) do {pay_rate_input, params} = split_pay_params(params) changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.change_job(socket.assigns.job, params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:pay_rate_input, pay_rate_input) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :job))} end def handle_event("validate", %{"assignment" => params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.change_job(socket.assigns.job, params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :assignment))} end # `:edit`, from the board's per-job "Edit" button: reschedule and/or # price change, staying put on the board. def handle_event("save", %{"job" => params}, %{assigns: %{action: :edit}} = socket) do {pay_rate_input, params} = split_pay_params(params) socket = assign(socket, :pay_rate_input, pay_rate_input) case Scheduling.update_job(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.job, params) do {:ok, job} -> notify_parent({:job_updated, job}) {:noreply, socket} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :job))} end end # `:quick_new`, from the board's own "New Job" button: same create as # `:new`, but notifies the parent instead of navigating away, so the # new job's brief shows up right there on the board. def handle_event("save", %{"job" => params}, %{assigns: %{action: :quick_new}} = socket) do {pay_rate_input, params} = split_pay_params(params) socket = assign(socket, :pay_rate_input, pay_rate_input) case Scheduling.create_job(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, job} -> notify_parent({:job_created, job}) {:noreply, socket} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :job))} end end # Navigates to the new job's show page directly (rather than # notifying the parent to decide) — a redirect issued from a parent's # `handle_info` in reaction to a component message lands one message # round-trip too late for `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_submit/1` to # observe it as a live redirect, which the board's own spex relies on. def handle_event("save", %{"job" => params}, socket) do {pay_rate_input, params} = split_pay_params(params) socket = assign(socket, :pay_rate_input, pay_rate_input) case Scheduling.create_job(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, job} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/schedule/jobs/#{job.id}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :job))} end end def handle_event("save", %{"assignment" => %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}}, socket) do case Scheduling.assign_cleaner( socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.job, parse_id(cleaner_id) ) do {:ok, job} -> notify_parent({:saved, job}) {:noreply, assign(socket, :conflict_error, nil)} {:error, :unavailable} -> {:noreply, assign( socket, :conflict_error, "This assignment has a scheduling conflict: the cleaner is unavailable that day." )} {:error, :overlap} -> {:noreply, assign( socket, :conflict_error, "This assignment was rejected: it overlaps another booking for this cleaner." )} end end defp parse_id(""), do: nil defp parse_id(nil), do: nil defp parse_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id) defp parse_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do Property |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) |> Repo.all() end defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) defp pay_type_options, do: [{"Hourly", "hourly"}, {"Piece rate", "piece_rate"}] defp pay_type_value(form) do case form[:pay_type].value do nil -> "" value -> to_string(value) end end # `hourly_rate`/`piece_rate` aren't real `Job` fields (only the # `_cents` columns are), so there's nothing on the changeset to # source a freshly-loaded job's dollar display from — this mirrors # `with_display_price/1` above, computed straight off whichever # `_cents` field matches the job's `pay_type`. defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: cents}) when is_integer(cents), do: cents_to_dollars(cents) defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents}) when is_integer(cents), do: cents_to_dollars(cents) defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{}), do: "" defp cents_to_dollars(cents), do: cents |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100)) |> Decimal.to_string(:normal) # Pulls the submitted dollar rate back out for redisplay (there's no # changeset field to read it from, per `initial_pay_rate_input/1` # above) and rewrites the matching `job[params]` key to # `*_rate_cents` before the changeset ever sees it — clearing the # other pay type's rate so switching pay types doesn't leave a # stale, unused rate behind. defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => "hourly", "hourly_rate" => dollars} = params) do {dollars, params |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", dollars_to_cents(dollars)) |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", nil)} end defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => "piece_rate", "piece_rate" => dollars} = params) do {dollars, params |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", dollars_to_cents(dollars)) |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", nil)} end defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => ""} = params) do {"", params |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", nil) |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", nil)} end defp split_pay_params(params), do: {"", params} # An unparseable dollar amount (or a blank input) becomes `nil` # rather than a changeset error — the rate is optional at the schema # level, same as `agreed_price`, so an invalid entry is treated as # "not set yet" rather than blocking the rest of the form. defp dollars_to_cents(dollars) when is_binary(dollars) do case Decimal.parse(String.trim(dollars)) do {decimal, ""} -> decimal |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer() _ -> nil end end defp dollars_to_cents(_dollars), do: nil defp field_errors(field) do if Phoenix.Component.used_input?(field), do: Enum.map(field.errors, &translate_error/1), else: [] end end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive do @moduledoc """ The owner's view of a pay period: every job with time recorded, what each cleaner is owed, which entries still need a clock-out before payroll can go out, and the CSV export. Route: `/timesheets`. """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Timesheet <:subtitle> {Date.to_string(elem(@period, 0))} – {Date.to_string(elem(@period, 1))} <:actions> <.button data-test="export-csv-button" phx-click="export" disabled={@unresolved?}> Export CSV

Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting.

{cleaner.name || cleaner.email}

Pay period total: {Money.format_cents(Map.get(@cleaner_totals, cleaner.id, 0))}

  • {cleaner.email} {Money.format_cents(summary.cents)} Missing clock-out <.form for={@resolve_form} id={"resolve-form-#{summary.job.id}"} data-test={"resolve-clock-out-form-#{summary.job.id}"} phx-submit="resolve_clock_out" > <.input type="time" name="time_entry[clock_out_time]" value="" label="Clock-out time" /> <.button phx-disable-with="Resolving...">Resolve Pay type not set for this job
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope period = TimeTracking.current_pay_period(scope) {:ok, socket |> assign(:resolve_form, to_form(%{}, as: :time_entry)) |> assign_period(scope, period)} end defp assign_period(socket, scope, period) do job_summaries = TimeTracking.list_job_time_summaries(scope, period) assign(socket, period: period, job_summaries: job_summaries, cleaners: job_summaries |> Enum.map(& &1.cleaner) |> Enum.uniq_by(& &1.id), cleaner_totals: TimeTracking.cleaner_pay_totals(scope, period), unresolved?: Enum.any?(job_summaries, & &1.unresolved?) ) end defp cleaner_summaries(job_summaries, cleaner) do Enum.filter(job_summaries, &(&1.cleaner.id == cleaner.id)) end @impl true def handle_event("export", _params, %{assigns: %{unresolved?: true}} = socket) do {:noreply, socket} end def handle_event("export", _params, socket) do {start_date, end_date} = socket.assigns.period {:noreply, redirect(socket, to: ~p"/timesheets/export?start_date=#{Date.to_iso8601(start_date)}&end_date=#{Date.to_iso8601(end_date)}" )} end def handle_event("resolve_clock_out", %{"time_entry" => %{"job_id" => job_id} = params}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id) socket = case TimeTracking.open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do nil -> socket entry -> case TimeTracking.resolve_clock_out(scope, entry, params) do {:ok, _entry} -> assign_period(socket, scope, socket.assigns.period) {:error, _changeset} -> socket end end {:noreply, socket} end end

content.text: Let's begin. First, login as owner and check the current timesheet state.

input.command: psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select id, status, pay_type, hourly_rate_cents, piece_rate_cents, cleaner_id from jobs where id in ('48ae34be-eb88-489b-9bd5-331476a9307b','51ef260f-90db-4357-9403-ea3574f9bac2','bb40913a-e5b1-44f2-af4e-fa46520781d8');" 2>&1

psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select job_id, clocked_in_at, clocked_out_at from time_entries where job_id in ('48ae34be-eb88-489b-9bd5-331476a9307b','51ef260f-90db-4357-9403-ea3574f9bac2','bb40913a-e5b1-44f2-af4e-fa46520781d8');" 2>&1

content.text: Now let's go to the schedule board and set pay types on the existing jobs, then create fresh hourly and piece-rate test jobs.
Good, the edit form now opens correctly. Let's set the pay type and rate.

input.command: psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select id, pay_type, hourly_rate_cents from jobs where id = '48ae34be-eb88-489b-9bd5-331476a9307b';" 2>&1

content.text: Confirmed working. Now let's do the same for the second existing job.

input.command: psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select id, pay_type, piece_rate_cents from jobs where id = '51ef260f-90db-4357-9403-ea3574f9bac2';" 2>&1

content.text: Both existing jobs now have pay resolved. Now let's create two fresh test jobs — one hourly, one piece-rate.
Now let's save this hourly job.

input.command: psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select id, pay_type, hourly_rate_cents, cleaner_id, scheduled_date from jobs where pay_type = 'hourly' and cleaner_id = 2 order by inserted_at desc limit 3;" 2>&1

content.text: Hourly job created: `e604cc04-c345-4638-9476-cfdbab3c33a6`, $25/hr. Now let's create the piece-rate job.

input.command: psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select id, pay_type, piece_rate_cents, cleaner_id, scheduled_date from jobs where pay_type = 'piece_rate' and cleaner_id = 2 order by inserted_at desc limit 3;" 2>&1

content.text: Piece-rate job created: `7a048bd4-c474-4d50-a4bd-7e5bdc74f27d`, $80 flat. Now let's log in as the cleaner and clock in on both jobs.
Now let's clock in on the hourly job (we'll leave it open so the owner can set a precise clock-out time later for exact duration control).

input.command: psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select job_id, clocked_in_at, clocked_out_at from time_entries where job_id = 'e604cc04-c345-4638-9476-cfdbab3c33a6';" 2>&1
psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select job_id, clocked_in_at, clocked_out_at from time_entries where job_id = 'e604cc04-c345-4638-9476-cfdbab3c33a6';" 2>&1

content.text: Clock-in worked. Now let's clock in and out on the piece-rate job (duration doesn't matter for piece-rate pay).

content.text:
I've paused testing and escalated to the team lead. Here's the current state:

**Just found:** The environment instability is broader than a single route. After the earlier login-page crash was fixed, I hit a new crash on one specific job page (`Protocol.UndefinedError` on `CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistTemplate`, reproducible 3/3 times) while an adjacent, nearly identical job page worked fine. While investigating that, the root page (`/`) itself started 500ing too, with a different missing module (`CleanerCrmWeb.PageController`). I confirmed both via curl, not just the browser, so it's not a session artifact.

This pattern — different, seemingly arbitrary modules intermittently "not available" — points to the running server having a partially-loaded or inconsistent build, not something for me to work around by retrying or restructuring my test approach. I've reported this to the team lead and am holding off on further 838/840 testing until they confirm the app is stable.

**Progress made on story 838 before the instability resurfaced**, worth preserving:
- Confirmed the new pay-type UI works: edited two pre-existing jobs (`48ae34be`, `51ef260f`) through the schedule board's Edit form to set `pay_type=hourly` ($20/hr) and `pay_type=piece_rate` ($45) respectively — both persisted correctly.
- Created two fresh test jobs via "New Job": `e604cc04` (hourly, $25/hr, assigned to qa-cleaner) and `7a048bd4` (piece-rate, $80) — the piece-rate one is the job now hitting the ChecklistTemplate crash.
- Clocked in as the cleaner on `e604cc04` (hourly job); it's currently sitting with an open time entry (clocked in at 13:37:18), ready for the owner to resolve to a precise clock-out time once things are stable again, to verify the rate × hours math.
- Job `51ef260f` (piece-rate $45, already has a long-elapsed resolved time entry from earlier testing) is a ready-made case for proving "piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time."

Once the team lead confirms the app is stable, the remaining work is: resolve `e604cc04`'s clock-out for the hourly-pay check, verify `51ef260f`'s piece-rate pay, check the running pay-period total across both, and verify CSV export now succeeds (or is correctly blocked) — then submit a fresh story 838 attempt, and go back to click-verify the story 840 reschedule/price-change scenarios I'd only code-reviewed.

#!/bin/bash
# Session-authenticated curl for Cleaner CRM QA.
# Usage: authenticated_curl.sh [email] [password] <curl-args...>
#   authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings
#   authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /users/settings -i
# Logs in via POST /users/log-in, stores the session cookie, then runs curl
# with the session against BASE_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:4100).
set -u

BASE_URL="${BASE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:4100}"
EMAIL="qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"
PASSWORD="qa password 1234"

if [[ "${1:-}" == *"@"* ]]; then
  EMAIL="$1"; PASSWORD="$2"; shift 2
fi

JAR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cleaner_crm_qa_cookies_$$"
trap 'rm -f "$JAR"' EXIT

page=$(curl -sS -c "$JAR" "$BASE_URL/users/log-in")
csrf=$(echo "$page" | grep -oE 'name="_csrf_token"[^>]*value="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*value="//;s/"$//')

login_code=$(curl -sS -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "$BASE_URL/users/log-in" -d "_csrf_token=$csrf" --data-urlencode "user[email]=$EMAIL" --data-urlencode "user[password]=$PASSWORD")

if [ "$login_code" != "302" ]; then
  echo "login failed with HTTP $login_code for $EMAIL" >&2
  exit 1
fi

path="$1"; shift
curl -sS -b "$JAR" "$@" "$BASE_URL$path"

# Qa Story Brief

## Tool

web

## Auth

Login at http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in (password form, second `<form>` on the
page, id `login_form_password` — the first form is magic-link and shares the same
`user[email]` field name, so scope selectors to `#login_form_password`).

- Owner: `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`
- Cleaner: `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`

Submit buttons are `button` elements with no stable selector other than text
("Log in and stay logged in →"); match by textContent rather than CSS.

## Seeds

Existing QA seed data. Cleaner `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` is user id 2, with
two jobs today (2026-07-08) at /field/jobs/48ae34be-eb88-489b-9bd5-331476a9307b
and /field/jobs/51ef260f-90db-4357-9403-ea3574f9bac2. No job in the dev DB has
`pay_type` set (see Finding below) — none needed seeding for the reachable
scenarios.

## What To Test

- Cleaner clocks in/out of an assigned job (criterion 7121): /field/jobs/:id,
  `[data-test="clock-in-button"]` then `[data-test="clock-out-button"]`.
- Cleaner opens a job not assigned to them (criterion 7123): direct navigation
  to another cleaner's /field/jobs/:id should redirect to /field with flash
  "This job is not assigned to you." and record no time entry.
- Owner reviews /timesheets: pay-period totals, unresolved-entry flagging,
  resolve-clock-out form, CSV export button disabled state (criteria
  7130, 7137, 7140).
- Hourly pay, piece-rate pay, CSV export success path (criteria 7125, 7128,
  7134): **blocked** — see Finding below.

## Result Path

Findings filed via create_issue; outcome via submit_qa_result (this file is
not the canonical record).

## Setup Notes

**Finding, not a config gap**: no page anywhere in the app (job creation, job
edit, or any settings page) exposes `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/
`piece_rate_cents` on a job, and `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.PayRate` (a
per-cleaner default rate) has zero references in `lib/cleaner_crm_web`. Every
job's pay is therefore permanently uncomputable, which cascades into the
timesheet always showing $0.00 totals, every job displayed as "Missing
clock-out" regardless of actual clock state, and CSV export permanently
disabled. Filed as issues a9233027 (critical) and e3d5222b (high). This
blocks 4 of 8 acceptance criteria from being exercised end-to-end; a future
QA pass should re-test 7125/7128/7130/7134 once pay-type entry ships.

scenarios.name: Cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job
scenarios.observation: Verified this pass and in the prior attempt (code path unchanged by the fixes): clocking in/out on an assigned job creates a real time_entries row with correct clocked_in_at/clocked_out_at.

scenarios.name: Cleaner tries to clock in on a job not assigned to them
scenarios.observation: Verified this pass and in the prior attempt (code path unchanged): navigating to another cleaner's job redirects to /field with flash 'This job is not assigned to you.'; no time entry recorded.

scenarios.name: Hourly job pays rate times worked hours
scenarios.observation: New job e604cc04 created via /schedule's New Job form with the new pay_type=hourly + hourly_rate fields ($25/hr). Clocked in at 13:37:18.208575, resolved via owner's timesheet to 16:07:00 (2.494942h). Displayed pay: $62.37, exactly matching round(2500 cents * 2.494942) = 6237 cents.

scenarios.name: Per-job piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time
scenarios.observation: Edited existing job 51ef260f to pay_type=piece_rate, piece_rate_cents=4500 via the Edit form. Its time entry spans ~22.51 hours (an artifact of an earlier resolve), yet displayed pay is exactly $45.00 flat, unaffected by the recorded duration.

scenarios.name: Running pay-period total builds as jobs complete
scenarios.observation: Cleaner pay-period total was $45.06 (job 48ae34be $0.06 + job 51ef260f $45.00) while e604cc04 was still open/excluded. After resolving e604cc04's clock-out, the total became $107.43 -- exactly $45.06 + $62.37, confirming the total builds correctly as each job resolves.

scenarios.name: Owner exports a completed pay period to CSV
scenarios.observation: Once all 3 jobs were resolved, GET /timesheets/export?start_date=2026-07-06&end_date=2026-07-12 (via authenticated_curl.sh) returned content-type text/csv, filename payroll-2026-07-06-2026-07-12.csv, body: 'cleaner_email,hours,job_count,gross_pay' / 'qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test,25.01,3,$107.43' -- hours (25.01) matches the sum of all 3 entries' worked hours computed directly from the DB timestamps.

scenarios.name: Cleaner forgets to clock out
scenarios.observation: e604cc04's time entry was left open after clock-in. Owner's /timesheets flagged it distinctly as 'Missing clock-out' with a resolve form (correctly NOT conflated with the separate 'Pay type not set' case now that both are distinguished), excluded it from the pay total, and successfully resolved it via the form to set an exact clock-out time.

scenarios.name: Export blocked while an unresolved time entry remains
scenarios.observation: Export CSV button was disabled with the warning 'Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting' while e604cc04 was open. Immediately after resolving it, the button became enabled and the export succeeded (see CSV export scenario above) -- full contrast now demonstrable, unlike the prior attempt where every job was permanently unresolved.

content.text: This reveals a significant new finding: `/schedule` and `/timesheets` have no owner/admin role check at all — I was actually logged in as the cleaner (not owner) this whole time, yet could freely reschedule jobs and access payroll data. Let me confirm this precisely, then continue testing as the correctly-authenticated owner.

input.command: grep -n "owner?\|require_authenticated\|on_mount" /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/index.ex /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/timesheet_live.ex 2>&1

input.title: /schedule and /timesheets have no owner/admin role check — any authenticated cleaner can reschedule jobs, change prices, and export payroll
input.description:
Discovered while live-testing story 840's reschedule/price-change audit scenarios: I intended to be logged in as qa-owner but the login page's "reauthenticate" flow silently re-authenticated my existing qa-cleaner session instead (a UX trap of its own, since the pre-filled/readonly email field doesn't make it obvious which account you're about to log back into). Without noticing, I performed a job reschedule as qa-cleaner (a plain field cleaner, not owner/admin) via /schedule's Edit form, and it succeeded -- audit entry confirms actor_id=2 (qa-cleaner), action=job_rescheduled.

Checked the router (lib/cleaner_crm_web/router.ex): both `/schedule` (and every ScheduleLive route -- job create/edit/reschedule/price-change/cancel/delete, recurring plan creation, cleaner management) and `/timesheets` live under the generic `:require_authenticated_user` live_session, which only checks "is logged in," not role. Confirmed via grep that neither `ScheduleLive.Index` nor `TimesheetLive` contains any `owner?`/role check anywhere in their source -- unlike `AuditLive`, which explicitly gates on `Accounts.get_user_role(...) == :owner` in its own `mount/3`.

Practical impact, all confirmed live as the qa-cleaner account: reschedule any job (including ones assigned to other cleaners), change any job's price, cancel/delete any job, create new jobs and recurring plans, view every cleaner's pay-period totals, resolve another cleaner's missing clock-out, and export the full payroll CSV for the whole account. This directly undermines story 840's own stated purpose ("hold my office team accountable") -- a field cleaner is exactly the kind of actor an owner would want audited and restricted, not handed office-manager-level scheduling and payroll access by default.

scenarios.name: Office staff reschedules a job and it is logged
scenarios.observation: Changed job 71182268's start/end time via /schedule's Edit form (09:00-11:00 -> 13:00-15:00). Resulting audit_entries row: action=job_rescheduled, old_value={end_time:11:00:00,start_time:09:00:00}, new_value={end_time:15:00:00,start_time:13:00:00}, correctly timestamped and attributed to the acting user. /audit renders it as '<actor> rescheduled Jamie Rivera QA1 ... Start time: 09:00:00 -> 13:00:00 / End time: 11:00:00 -> 15:00:00'.

scenarios.name: Price change records old and new value
scenarios.observation: Set the same job's price nil->$120, then $120->$140 in two separate saves. Two job_price_changed rows: old={agreed_price_cents:null}/new={agreed_price_cents:12000}, then old={agreed_price_cents:12000}/new={agreed_price_cents:14000}. Neither row includes scheduled_date/start_time/end_time despite the job having those fields too -- confirms only the changed field is captured. /audit renders 'Price: -- to $120.00' and 'Price: $120.00 to $140.00'.

scenarios.name: Nobody can alter or delete an audit entry
scenarios.observation: Unchanged from prior attempt: verified via code (Audit.Recorder exposes no update/delete function anywhere, AuditLive's render has no edit/delete affordance) and via the migration (20260707180010_create_audit_entries_table.exs) which adds Postgres RULEs audit_entries_no_update/audit_entries_no_delete that both DO INSTEAD NOTHING -- defense in depth even against raw SQL. Did not attempt a live destructive UPDATE/DELETE against a real row; correctly declined as an unauthorized mutation of shared dev data, and code+migration evidence is conclusive on its own.

scenarios.name: Owner filters the trail to find who moved a job
scenarios.observation: The filter form now has a 'Changed by' select (every account member plus System) and a 'Record type' select (Job/Property/Quote), alongside the existing Subject ID and From/To date fields. Selecting actor=qa-cleaner correctly narrowed the trail to exactly qa-cleaner's 4 entries. Combining actor=qa-cleaner with record type=Property correctly returned zero rows (qa-cleaner has only ever touched Job records), confirming the filters combine with AND logic. Previously-filed issue fb8da672 is resolved.

scenarios.name: Automated recurring job generation is attributed to the system
scenarios.observation: Unchanged from prior attempt: created a recurring plan via /schedule/plans/new; all 3 generated jobs got audit_entries with system=true, actor_id=null, action=job_created, and /audit correctly rendered them as 'System created ...' rather than a blank actor.
